Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Ruby gem install stripe sinatra 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.RB Copy Showing Ruby require "sinatra" require "stripe" Stripe.api_key = ENV.fetch("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY") post "/create-checkout-session" do session = Stripe::Checkout::Session.create( line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, } ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) redirect session.url, 303 end Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends using saved Price objects whenever practical. mode Use payment for one-time purchases, subscription for recurring billing, or setup to collect a reu

That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.RB Copy Showing Ruby require "sinatra" require "stripe" Stripe.api_key = ENV.fetch("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY") post "/create-checkout-session" do session = Stripe::Checkout::Session.create( line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, } ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) redirect session.url, 303 end Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends using saved Price objects whenever practical. mode Use payment for one-time purchases, subscription for recurring billing, or setup to collect a reu
